papers.title_in_file: Efﬁcient quasi-phase-matched frequency conversion in a lithium niobate racetrack microresonator
papers.what_it_is: A short conference-style report of second harmonic generation in a periodically poled lithium niobate on insulator racetrack microresonator, with a normalized efficiency of about 3.8% per mW.

assertions.value: The authors report a device fabricated on an X-cut magnesium-doped LNOI wafer, which is a 500-nm thick LN thin film bonded on a 2-µm thermally grown silicon dioxide layer above a silicon substrate.
quotes: The device is fabricated on a X-cut magnesium-doped LNOI wafer (NANOLN Inc.), which is a 500-nm thick LN thin
bonded on 2-µm thermally grown silicon dioxide layer above a silicon substrate
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device platform in Section 2, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the magnesium-doped thin film is used to mitigate the photorefractive effect induced by the intense optical field of highly confined pump power.
quotes: Magnesium doped thin ﬁlm is used to mitigate photorefractive effect induced by intense optical ﬁeld of highly conﬁned pump power.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors give the purpose of their own material choice in Section 2, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that an additional EBL process defines the racetrack microresonator structure after the poling region is created by the process of their reference 5, and that a standard ion-milling process (references 6 and 7) gives the microresonators.
quotes: First, we use the similar process (as described in [5]) to create the poling region as shown in Fig. 1(a).
Then, additional EBL process is carried out to deﬁne the racetrack microresonator structure.
by carrying out a standard ion-milling process [6, 7]
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper describes its own fabrication steps in Section 2, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors report a waveguide top-width of 1.8 µm, a straight waveguide length of 300 µm and a half-ring radius of 120 µm for the racetrack device, with the poling pattern in one straight waveguide.
quotes: Waveguide top-width is 1.8 µm. The length of the straight waveguide is 300 µm and the radius of the half-ring is 120 µm.
Yellow region is the poling pattern for one straight waveguide within the racetrack microresonator.
assertions.certainty_reason: Device dimensions are stated in the Figure 1 caption.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for X-cut orientation, they use quasi-TE (TE00) mode interaction to access the largest nonlinear coefficient d33, about 27 pm/V.
quotes: we utilize quasi-traverse-electric (TE00) modes interaction to access the largest nonlinear
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own design choice in Section 2, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that phase matching in the racetrack requires quasi-phase matching in the PPLN section and also doubly-resonance for both the pump and the signal cavity modes, and that the global chip temperature is varied to compensate the resonance mismatch between the two modes caused by different thermo-optic coefficients.
quotes: To satisfy the phase matching condition in this racetrack microresonator, we not only need to ful
but also to achieve doubly-resonance for both pump and signal cavity modes.
Due to different thermaloptic coe
we can vary the global temperature of the chip to compensate their resonance mismatch.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own phase matching condition and tuning method in Section 2, p.1.
assertions.reader_inference: The first and third quotes are cut before a ligature character the text layer holds, so each ends inside a word.

assertions.value: The authors report racetrack microresonators with an intrinsic quality factor Q0 of about 5.3 × 105 (printed flat in the text layer; ten to the fifth power) and an extracted average propagation loss of 0.7 dB/cm.
quotes: Then we obtain the high-Q racetrack microresonators (Q0 ≈ 5.3 × 105, see Fig. 1 (c))
with extracted average propagation loss to be 0.7dB/cm.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper does not say how Q0 was extracted beyond a reference to Fig. 1(c); it is a single device's value.

assertions.value: The authors report a continuous-wave tunable pump laser (Santec 550, 1500-1630 nm) with a fiber polarization controller, and two tapered fibers (2 µm spot diameter) as input and output couplers with losses of 5 dB per facet at 1600 nm and 6 dB per facet at 800 nm.
quotes: we use continuous-wave tunable laser (Santec 550, 1500-1630 nm) as pump laser
(2 µm spot diameter, OZ optics)
with losses of 5 dB per facet at 1600 nm and 6 dB per facet at 800 nm, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own measurement setup in Section 2, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors report that, after sweeping the infrared laser and scanning the temperature, they identify an optimal cavity mode at 1605.199 nm at 34.2◦C, and that for 1.1 mW pump power in the input fiber they collect 700 nW SH power in the output fiber via a visible power meter.
quotes: we identify an optimal cavity mode (i.e. 1605.199 nm at 34.2
For 1.1 mW pump power in the input
we collect 700 nW SH power in the output
assertions.reader_inference: The last two quotes are cut before the ligature character in the word fiber, so each ends before it.

assertions.value: The authors report an estimated coupled-in pump power of 270 µW and an estimated on-chip SH power of 2.79 µW, which they state corresponds to a normalized SHG efficiency of 3.8% mW −1, using the coupling loss and near critical coupling for the infrared cavity mode (about 7 dB deep).
quotes: Considering the coupling loss and near critical coupling for infrared cavity mode (∼ 7dB deep)
the estimated coupled-in pump power and on-chip SH power are 270 µW and 2.79 µW, respectively.
assertions.reader_inference: The on-chip values are estimates from fiber-end powers and assumed coupling losses, not direct on-chip measurements. 2.79 µW divided by the square of 0.270 mW is about 3.8% per mW, consistent with the stated figure.

assertions.value: The authors report an observed normalized SHG conversion efficiency of about 3.8% mW −1 in a quasi-phase-matched racetrack microresonator with Q0 of about 5.3 × 105.
quotes: The observed normalized conversion efﬁciency is about 3.8% mW −1.
assertions.reader_inference: A single mode of a single device; no device-to-device statistics are given.

assertions.value: The authors report that, scanning the pump power within a few tens of micro-watts to avoid thermal effect, the generated SH power shows a nearly quadratic response with slope about 2.2 (Fig. 2(a)).
quotes: To avoid thermal effect in this high-Q microresonator,
we scan the pump power within few tens of micro-watts and collect the generated SH power.
It shows nearly quadratic response (∼ slope 2.2) as shown in Fig. 2(a).
assertions.reader_inference: The slope value is read from the text; the figure data are not in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors report that the temperature dependency of the SH power for the optimized cavity mode has a 3 dB bandwidth of less than 1◦C, which they state indicates a stringent requirement for meeting the doubly-resonant condition with high-Q resonances.
quotes: its 3 dB bandwidth is less than 1◦C, which indicates the stringent requirement for meeting doubly-resonant condition with high-Q resonances.

assertions.value: The authors report a microscope image of SHG in the racetrack microresonator with 100 µW on-chip pump power, and state that more scattered SH light is observed in the periodically poled straight waveguide due to higher loss in that section.
quotes: (e) Microscope image of SHG in the racetrack microresonator with 100 µW on-chip pump power.
More scattered SH light is observed due to higher loss in this section.

assertions.value: The authors claim to demonstrate for the first time efficient second harmonic generation in a quasi-phasematched high-Q racetrack microresonator with fundamental-modes matching.
quotes: Here, we demonstrate for the ﬁrst time, efﬁcient second harmonic generation in a quasi-phasematched high-Q (Q0 ≈ 5.3 × 105) racetrack microresonator with fundamental-modes matching.
assertions.reader_inference: A priority claim by the authors; not checked against other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the recorded normalized conversion efficiency of 3.8% mW −1 is more than 40 times higher than a recently reported quasi-phase-matched lithium niobate microring (their reference 4).
quotes: The recorded normalized conversion efﬁciency is 3.8% mW −1, which is more than 40 times higher than recently reported quasiphase-matched lithium niobate microring [4].
assertions.reader_inference: The compared figure from reference 4 is not given in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that high-order modal phase matching is limited by a relatively low Q (about 105, printed flat; ten to the fifth power), due to the required narrow waveguide width of about 700 nm, and by poor mode overlapping (below 10%).
quotes: the former’s performance is limited by its relatively low Q (∼ 105, due to the required narrow waveguide width ∼ 700nm for achieving phase matching) and the poor mode overlapping (< 10%).

assertions.value: The authors state that cyclic phase matching is limited by the highly restricted mode overlapping between the fundamental (pump) and fifth-order (second harmonic) modes.
quotes: While the latter is limited by the highly restricted mode overlapping between fundamental (pump) and ﬁfth-order (second harmonic) modes.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they realized efficient second harmonic generation in an optimally mode-matched, high-Q racetrack microresonator that is partially poled on chip, reaching an SHG efficiency as high as 3.8% mW −1 by cavity enhancement.
quotes: we have realized efﬁcient second harmonic generation in an optimally mode-matched, high-Q racetrack microresonator that is partially poled on chip.
we achieved SHG efﬁciency as high as 3.8% mW −1.

assertions.value: The authors state that adding a micro-heater on top of the microresonator will allow them to tune and lock the doubly-resonant condition of the fundamental and second harmonic modes in the near future.
quotes: adding a micro-heater on top of the microresonator will allow us to tune and lock doubly-resonant of fundamental and second harmonic modes the near future.
assertions.reader_inference: Planned work, not demonstrated in this paper; it implies the present device has no on-chip tuning.

assertions.value: The authors claim that their implementation of PPLN within a racetrack microresonator could enable a multitude of applications, such as quantum light generation and optical parametric amplification in integrated photonics circuits.
quotes: could enable a multitude of applications, such as quantum light generation and optical parametric ampliﬁcation in integrated photonics circuits.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum light generation is demonstrated in this paper; the measurement is classical SHG with a CW pump.
